newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NBP evaluates banks for 1998 dealer status.
newsitem.headline: Polish NBP evaluates banks for 1998 dealer status.

text.p: The Polish central bank began a nine-month scheme on Wednesday to evaluate banks seeking money market dealer status in 1998, the central bank said.

"From March 1, 1997, the National Bank of Poland (NBP) started evaluating banks-candidates for money market dealer status in 1998," the NBP said in a letter sent to Polish commercial banks' presidents.
In 1998 money market dealers will be allowed to participate in the NBP's repos and reverse repos, in primary NBP-bill sales and would relish higher presitige.
In 1997 the central bank awarded the money market dealer status to 17 banks.

Those who want to obtain the status will be evaluated in terms of the amount of T-bills sold to non-banking domestic investors, their market share in secondary T-bill and NBP-bill trade and service quality.
A bank can win the largest number of points for building up clients' T-bill portfolios.
